minutes.headline: Selectmen endorsed the draft housing production plan, set a Jan. 13 Whitetail Crossing road hearing, and renewed 2015 licenses.
minutes.summary: The board appointed a new Historical Commission member, scheduled a road acceptance hearing for Whitetail Crossing and referred it to the planning board, and approved the 2015 business and alcohol licenses category by category. It endorsed the draft housing production plan with comments to be incorporated, and discussed the earth removal bylaw ahead of a workshop. Committee reports covered school technology device options and school budget requests.

public_comment.topic: Questioned whether the earth removal bylaw's 10 cubic yard threshold is too low and described tiered permitting used elsewhere.

what_happened.line: The Select Board endorsed the draft housing production plan, with board, Mrs Bertram's and the state's comments to be incorporated, with none opposed.
The board scheduled a January 13, 2015 hearing on accepting Whitetail Crossing as a town road and referred it to the planning board.
The board approved the 2015 alcohol, common victualer, amusement, entertainment, motor vehicle, limousine and peddler licenses category by category, none opposed.
The board appointed a new member to the Historical Commission, with none opposed.
A workshop on earth removal and gravel permitting is planned for January or February, possibly leading to a spring town meeting bylaw.

why_it_matters: Accepting Whitetail Crossing would make the town responsible for maintaining that road, a cost that falls on the town budget, mostly taxes.
The earth removal workshop could lead to a bylaw that residents would be asked to vote on at a spring town meeting, changing which gravel and soil work needs a permit.
School technology device options for grades 10-12 would add IT staffing and possible fees for families, and school budget requests will feed into the coming budget.
